A Time of War : A Memoir Across Three Generations

Dear reader, it is with great excitement that I offer this expansive work for your consideration: A recently unearthed, voluminous manuscript – an epic memoir written over the course of three generations. It is a work as monumental and daunting as it is groundbreaking - a glimpse into the inner workings of the true scientific mind.

Upon discovery of these immaculate pages, I, suffering great personal expense, set forth to ensure the general publication and distribution of this important history. It is a work that will perhaps elucidate upon and justify the eccentric reputations of my forebears.

While I admit that I am biased in this appraisal, as it is my own exemplary lineage which is documented, I submit this comprehensive prosopography in as accurate a condition as I can muster. As one will soon attest, it is a chronicle of events of a decidedly fantastical nature, yet my research confirms it to be as true and vital a work as has ever been seen in print.

However, I must offer a word of caution to those with weaker constitutions. While these pages hold a brilliant catalogue of achievements, they also boldly depict the setbacks encountered along the journey. Gruesome, grim, and horrifying as they may be, I have included their spine-chilling contents as originally written. As one might expect, in exposing the base components of the universe, we uncover both light and darkness in equal measure. For without darkness, we cannot appreciate the brilliance of the light.
Taking Sides

My father was a genius! I state this now, not with the naïveté of my initial discovery of his journal, but as a time-tested statement of truth. It is why I pen these words today for posterity and to affirm with deep conviction what some may erroneously refer to as mad science.

When I first arrived at my father's manor, I carried the same skepticism any normal individual would. Weary as I was from the excursion across the Hungarian plains, the cold, gray walls of the villa with its oppressive iron gates chilled me to my marrow. When the disfigured caretaker — the only person privileged with the knowledge — revealed to me a false door and spiraling staircase that descended to a secret laboratory, the grim discovery did nothing to soothe my nerves. In fact, the sight of jars filled with preserved flesh and the astringent stench of chemicals aggravated my frail state, leaving me to take my suppers in the bedroom for several weeks.

But, it was this same dark discovery that eventually roused me from my illness. For as I pored over the journal bequeathed to me and surveyed page after page of formulaic experimentation, my apprehensions melted. I felt trepidacious, yet unreservedly enthusiastic at the ethical implications of this great task!

Yet even after the disquiet within my soul was relieved, the nearby village rattled my window panes with cacophonous revelry. At first, I kept my visits to the borough brief and infrequent. It seemed that whenever I turned my head I would lock eyes with a cautious observer, and I felt the entire town's steel gaze like daggers tickling the back of my skull. I could only speculate that my siblings endured the same sordid treatment.

It was my spouse, using my extended rest to become better acquainted with the village, who explained how spirited political discourse was the source of this commotion. Then I could discern the rally cry of their evening demonstrations as they spoke of disobedience, the end of monarchy, and civil war.

I began to realize the potential boon that war could provide for my research. If the people shared a mere fraction of the passion that now stoked the fires of my heart, how easily they would embrace my scientific assistance! While my father's ambitions were strong, his solitary existence had doomed his ideas to obscurity.

I would not repeat this error. I would brave the jeers of the populace to guide them in the art of warfare. My efforts would determine the course of this conflict. And when the time comes, it will be my science that will emerge from the flames of war as the true victor!
War on the Horizon

The spectre of war haunted the small village. This ideological tension would erupt in loud displays and gatherings of the peasantry near the Town Hall. For all the folderol, I began to cherish the moments when the eerie stillness of the evening was broken by anguished yells.

The Separatists felt alienated by the aristocratic government and wished to secede. Their brash tactics aimed to incite a democratic revolt among the proletariat. The Unified Monarchists feared the anarchic destabilization of the economy at such a key moment during industrialization. I was quickly able to determine that the town supported the {{0=...|Separatists|...}}.

A local farmer had observed my conversation, and after determining an agreeable moment to greet me, we engaged in a cordial chat about the local economy. The earthy individual even suggested a visit to his plantation, which turned out to be most advantageous.
Advancement of Knowledge

While it seemed anomalous to me at the time, when my conversation ended I was immediately greeted by a fellow who introduced himself as one who shared an affinity for the scientific. I was intrigued and invited the young man in the brown sack suit to dine with me at a local cafe. Admittedly, my university knowledge was the main course, but I was still able to glean a few novel tidbits.
Dashing Conversationalist

At university, I had always excelled at public speaking engagements. So when our conversation concluded, I spent the next few hours introducing myself to the less than charming group of locals that frequently attended political meetings. While they may not have fully comprehended the intelligence I exuded, there was certainly an air of cheerfulness when I exited the building.
Curious Individual

My intense curiosity was noted by the townspeople, and it appeared that my conversation with the vagrant had created a stir amongst the local gossips. I resolved to keep my meetings more clandestine in the future.
Military Protection

On a brisk April morning, my family was called upon to attend another Town Hall meeting. This time, however, the atmosphere was especially heated.

Being conscious of the dominant attitudes in town, I understood that the prevailing preference was for the {{0=...|Separatists|...}} forces. As influential members of the aristocratic establishment, it was inevitable that the military officers turned to us for support in building a barracks within the village. Oh what a frivolous distraction matters of politics prove to be!

The Town's Reaction

I was quite convinced that strengthening our relationship with the dominant faction and encouraging a route towards inevitable conflict would ensure a fresh demand for my experiments. If that sentiment aligned with the bedraggled populace, then so be it.

For reasons which I cannot fathom, our collective referendum was received with mild acceptance. While it stifled the construction temporarily, the town's allegiance remained unwavering.

Could it be that I had underestimated the scope of their ignorance? How was it that even under pressure from {{0=|two|three|four}} aristocratic financiers they remained apprehensive and defiant?
